hook: Under twenty percent down on a home?

blocks.narration: Under twenty percent down on a home? You will probably pay P M I. Good news: it can disappear.
blocks.visual: Tilt-shift miniature house with a small extra weight chained to its front door

blocks.narration: Private mortgage insurance protects the lender, not you, in case a borrower with a smaller down payment stops paying the loan.
blocks.visual: A tiny shield floats above a bank building on the miniature street, not above the house

blocks.narration: It is usually added to your monthly payment on a conventional loan, and it can add up to a meaningful amount each year.
blocks.visual: A small envelope from the house grows a little heavier each month

blocks.narration: Here is the key rule. As you pay down the loan, your loan-to-value ratio drops, meaning you owe less compared to the home's value.
blocks.visual: A small bar beside the house slowly lowers as coins are paid into it

blocks.narration: Under federal rules, you can generally ask your lender to cancel P M I once you reach eighty percent of the original value.
blocks.visual: A tiny hand rings a bell at the bank when the bar crosses a glowing line

blocks.narration: And it generally ends automatically when the scheduled balance reaches seventy-eight percent of the original value, if you are current on payments.
blocks.visual: The chain on the door clicks open on its own and falls away

blocks.narration: Extra payments toward principal can get you there sooner. Rising home values may also help, though lenders may require an appraisal.
blocks.visual: Extra coins drop into the bar while a tiny appraiser measures the house

blocks.narration: Find your eighty percent date on the amortization schedule and mark it. Share this with a friend house hunting right now.
blocks.visual: The house glows freely at golden hour, the weight gone, birds flying past

cta: Share this with a friend house hunting right now.

captions.hook_line: Putting less than 20% down? Here's how to get rid of PMI 🏠
captions.body: Conventional loans with under 20% down usually require private mortgage insurance. Under federal rules, you can generally ask to cancel PMI at 80% loan-to-value, and it generally ends automatically at 78% on the original schedule.

youtube_title: PMI Explained: The Fee That Can Disappear
